timing_position.description: The layer evaluates whether a proposed transition has standing before consequence attempts to bind.

admissibility_assertion.primary_assertion: Given the declared StegVerse governance boundary, visible authority class, policy reference, context state, review posture, and receipt conditions at commit time, this transition is admitted or denied by the StegVerse transition-admissibility layer.

observes: context state visible at commit time
assumes_but_does_not_independently_valid: truth of upstream evidence unless explicitly retained and checked by the layer
legal sufficiency of external authority assertions
continued downstream validity after the admitted transition
complete post-event evidentiary reconstruction outside retained artifacts
semantic equivalence between adjacent governance layers
non_claims: The layer does not claim universal admissibility.
The layer does not claim that all upstream governance sources were globally valid.
The layer does not claim that downstream consequences remain valid indefinitely.
The layer does not claim legal, regulatory, or organizational sufficiency outside its declared boundary.
The layer does not claim that discovery through an organization index creates authority inheritance.
The layer does not claim interoperability with GLM, EVIDE, or any adjacent governance system.
The layer does not claim complete post-event evidentiary reconstruction.

evidentiary_handoff.handoff_scope: Materials required to reconstruct what the StegVerse layer asserted at commit time.

visibility_ends_at: downstream systems that alter state after commit
evidentiary registries outside StegVerse unless explicitly referenced
adjacent governance layers that have not explicitly declared a composition relationship

five_question_boundary_model.what_does_the_layer_claim: It claims that a proposed transition is admitted or denied within the declared StegVerse transition-governance boundary at commit time.
five_question_boundary_model.what_does_the_layer_observe: It observes the transition request, authority class, policy reference, visible context state, review posture, receipt conditions, and commit-time validity result.
five_question_boundary_model.what_does_the_layer_assume: It may assume upstream evidence truth, external legal sufficiency, downstream continuity, and completeness of later reconstruction unless those matters are explicitly inside the declared boundary and supported by retained artifacts.
five_question_boundary_model.what_remains_reviewable: The transition receipt, authority class reference, policy reference, review posture, admissibility result, commit-time validity result, and retained replay materials may remain reviewable if preserved.
five_question_boundary_model.where_does_visibility_end: Visibility ends at unobserved upstream evidence, external authority systems, legal interpretations outside the declared boundary, downstream consequences after commit, and evidentiary registries not explicitly referenced by the StegVerse receipt structure.
